name: Reverse Dividend Arbitrage
summary: Short 100 shares plus a long call over the ex-dividend date, betting that the price drop on the ex-date exceeds the dividend the short position owes; the mirror of dividend arbitrage and equally closed by market pricing.

legs.strike_rule: n/a — short 100 shares before the ex-date
Deep ITM call, delta >= 0.90, minimal extrinsic

max_profit: (ex-date price drop - dividend_owed) x 100 - call_extrinsic x 100 - borrow_costs - fees. Expected value is negative because the drop averages approximately the dividend and the short owes the full amount.
max_loss: call_extrinsic x 100 + borrow_costs + fees, plus buy-in risk on the share leg
breakevens: Requires the ex-date drop to exceed the dividend by more than the call's extrinsic plus borrow plus fees.
when_to_use: Effectively never. The short share position owes the full declared dividend in cash on the payment date, and the ex-date price adjustment is on average equal to the dividend — so the structural edge is zero before costs and negative after borrow fees.
entry_rules: NOT VIABLE on this account. Requires shorting shares (borrow availability, borrow fee, buy-in risk) and paying away the dividend. Options side is Level 2 (long call only), so the block is the equity leg and the economics, not the approval level.
Required test if ever evaluated: expected_ex_date_drop - dividend - call_extrinsic - borrow_cost - fees > $0.05 per share. This test is not expected to pass.
Never on a special dividend — special dividends of 10%+ trigger OCC contract adjustments and the ex-date mechanics differ.
Alpaca paper short fills do not validate live borrow.
management_rules: If ever run: exit the entire structure on the ex-date open. Holding longer converts a dividend play into an unwanted short stock position.
Track the dividend liability explicitly — the cash is debited on the payment date, after the position is closed, so realised P/L lags.
exit_rules: No short option legs, so no option assignment exposure.
Close the long call by 15:00 ET on its expiration day if ITM; auto-exercise would buy 100 shares and close the short at the strike without a decision.
Close the short shares and the long call together, options leg first.
Exit immediately on any buy-in notice.
assignment_risk: No short options. The hazard is on the equity leg: short shares owe the dividend, and a hard-to-borrow buy-in can force the short to be covered at any time and any price.
buying_power: Reg T short stock (50% of proceeds) plus the call debit, plus borrow fees and the dividend liability.
liquidity_needs: Easy borrow is the binding requirement; deep ITM call bid-ask <= $0.05.
common_mistakes: Forgetting that the short pays the dividend. Assuming the ex-date drop exceeds the dividend systematically — it does not, and where it appears to, taxes and market microstructure explain the difference.
